subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
passage: The power went out at seven on Sunday evening, so Kiran and Saurabh sat with a phone torch and the paper planner. This was the weekly check. Kiran read the week aloud: two lab reports done, the statistics revision half done, the gym missed twice. "Why did the revision slip?" Saurabh asked. "Because I put it after the club meeting and I was tired." That was the signal. The unfinished revision moved to a morning slot next week. With only the torch battery to spare, Kiran also crossed out the second club meeting, since the week was already too full. The paper looked lighter. Saurabh took a photo for the shared list.

qa.q: At what time did the power go out on Sunday?
qa.a: The power went out at seven on Sunday evening.

qa.q: What did Kiran realise about why the revision slipped?
qa.a: Kiran realised that the revision had been put after the club meeting when Kiran was tired, so it needed a morning slot.

qa.q: What other approach could work if the plan is too full again next week?
qa.a: Kiran could pick the one commitment that matters least each Sunday and drop it early, since a lighter week is easier to keep.

qa.q: How might Saurabh see the weekly check?
qa.a: Saurabh probably finds it useful and calming, since the questions helped Kiran see the reason instead of just feeling guilty.

grounding: Each Sunday a student checks what was done and what slipped, moves unfinished items to next week and cuts a commitment when it is too full.
